reason: Adds E211 (shell without unsafe_shell = true), E212 (command and shell forms conflict), E213 (placeholder not a whole command element or inside shell text), W409 (unsafe_shell in use), W410 (cwd = untrusted-current) and W411 (script starts with #!/usr/bin/env). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text; no code is reused or deprecated.

W411 still means: the script a command segment would run is refused by its first line, so it will not run. It now reports every first line the executor refuses (the executor's own rule: `#!/usr/bin/env` or an interpreter that is /usr/bin/env under another name, a relative interpreter, a line over 256 bytes, a NUL), naming which in a new {reason} argument, where it named only the first case before; {id} and {path} keep their meaning and the fix is unchanged. Its number, status and severity stay; no code is reused or deprecated.

W404 still means: a user segment that needs a trusted layout is left out because no line of a trusted layout draws it. It now also covers env segments, which show the user's environment and take the same layout verdict as command segments, so its text says the segment is not used (an env segment does not run) and its explanation names command and env segments. {id} and the fix keep their meaning. Its number, status and severity stay; no code is reused or deprecated.

N502 is deprecated, not reused: it said a declared user segment of a kind the prompt does not draw yet would show after an upgrade. Language segments are now drawn, so every kind a segment can declare (text, command, env, language) is drawn and the condition can no longer arise; the compile step that emitted it is removed. Its number, severity and texts stay so an old report still reads. No other code changes, and no new code takes its place.

Adds the findings of `bingsu doctor`: W601 (a folder on the way to the executable can be changed by another user), W602 (the bingsu on PATH is not the running one), W603 (no folders pinned in this shell), E604 (a pinned folder is not the same now), W605 (the collector or prompt executable beside bingsu is missing or from another build), W606 (the kernel has no seccomp) and E607 (the settings have an error). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text; no code is reused or deprecated.

Adds E106 (a JSON settings file that does not parse, with the reader's {message}) and E308 (one place holds two settings files of different formats, naming both {path} and {other}). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text: E101 still means invalid TOML only, and E102-E105 already describe any config file. No code is reused or deprecated.

Removes a unit test from the registry file that refused the word `doctor` in a fix text, since the command exists now. No code is added, removed, reused or deprecated, and every code keeps its number, status, arguments and text.

Adds E107 (a YAML settings file that does not parse, or breaks a rule every settings file keeps: a key written twice in one mapping, `null` as a value, a top that is not a mapping; the reader's {message}) and E108 (a YAML feature bingsu does not read, named in {feature}: an anchor, an alias, a tag, a second document or a key that is a mapping or a list). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text: E101 still means invalid TOML only and E106 invalid JSON only; E102-E105 already describe any config file, including the size, encoding, integer range and nesting limits of a YAML file. No code is reused or deprecated.

Adds the shell-evidence findings of `bingsu doctor`: E608 (the shell's hook asks for a record version this bingsu does not read), W609 (the hook functions are not in the order bingsu needs), W610 (the last envelope words are not the expected ones) and W611 (the shell is older than 5.8). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text; no code is reused or deprecated.

Adds N504 (a note: at some widths a layout band draws its own template in place of [layout] lines that a file other than the built-in theme and other than the file of that template wrote; {band}, {widths} and {lines} name the band, the widths it is chosen at and the lines it replaces). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text: N501 still covers lines or options written in the same layout table as a template, and W407 a band no width chooses (N504 is never said for such a band). No code is reused or deprecated.

Adds the two terminal measurements of `bingsu doctor`: W613 (the terminal draws probe characters in other widths than the settings assume) and W614 (the terminal's background is the other brightness than the prompt draws for under `colors.mode = "auto"`). Every existing code keeps its number, status, arguments and text; no code is reused or deprecated.
